answer: PoA binds each identity to bonded collateral in escrow, but evaluates correlated equivocation across identities rather than treating each signer in isolation. If k coordinated identities equivocate, pairwise evidence creates O(k^2) penalty exposure; detection also applies an exponential multiplier to forfeiture, making a sybil swarm costlier than splitting one operator’s stake. Juniper, ferrous, and trellis labels may distinguish keys, but cannot erase shared-risk correlations or asymmetric capital depreciation.
